claims.quote: Such great issues, supposing them to be possible, as the return of Western Europe to the Roman communion, the overthrow of the British Empire by Germany
claims.description: Possible future upheavals such as Western Europe returning to Catholicism or Germany overthrowing the British Empire.

claims.quote: a highly mobile conveyance capable of travelling easily and swiftly to any desired point, traversing, at a reasonably controlled pace, the ordinary roads and streets, and having access for higher rates of speed and long-distance travelling to specialized ways restricted to swift traffic
claims.description: The ideal transport is a personal vehicle that drives on ordinary streets and also on dedicated high-speed roads for long trips.

claims.quote: Had such an ideal been kept in view from the first the traveller would now be able to get through his long-distance journeys at a pace of from seventy miles or more an hour without changing
claims.description: Had road vehicles been developed instead of railways, travelers would already go door to door at seventy miles an hour or more.

claims.quote: so far as a light powerful engine goes, comparatively noiseless, smooth-running, not obnoxious to sensitive nostrils, and altogether suitable for high road traffic, the problem will very speedily be solved.
claims.description: A light, powerful, quiet and clean engine for road vehicles will soon be perfected.

claims.quote: the numerous advantages of such an arrangement will lead to the organization of large carrier companies, using such motor trucks to carry goods in bulk or parcels on the high roads.
claims.description: Large trucking companies will haul freight and parcels by motor truck on the highways.

claims.quote: Such companies will be in an exceptionally favourable position to organize storage and repair for the motors of the general public on profitable terms
claims.description: Trucking firms will run garages offering storage and repair for private motorists.

claims.quote: In the next place, and parallel with the motor truck, there will develop the hired or privately owned motor carriage.
claims.description: Privately owned cars and hired cars (taxis) will become common.

claims.quote: It will be capable of a day's journey of three hundred miles or more, long before the developments to be presently foreshadowed arrive.
claims.description: A private motor car will be able to cover three hundred miles or more in a day.

claims.quote: One will be free to dine where one chooses, hurry when one chooses, travel asleep or awake, stop and pick flowers, turn over in bed of a morning and tell the carriage to wait—unless, which is highly probable, one sleeps aboard.
claims.description: Car owners will travel on their own schedule, likely sleeping in their vehicles (motor homes).

claims.quote: And thirdly there will be the motor omnibus, attacking or developing out of the horse omnibus companies and the suburban lines.
claims.description: Motor buses will replace horse buses and compete with suburban railways.

claims.quote: will secure the power to form private roads of a new sort, upon which their vehicles will be free to travel up to the limit of their very highest possible speed.
claims.description: Motor companies will build private motor-only roads where vehicles can drive at top speed, separated from horses and pedestrians.

claims.quote: And the quiet English citizen will, no doubt, while these things are still quite exceptional and experimental in his lagging land, read one day with surprise in the violently illustrated popular magazines of 1910, that there are now so many thousand miles of these roads already established in America and Germany and elsewhere.
claims.description: By 1910 America and Germany will have thousands of miles of motor roads while England lags behind.

claims.quote: Almost insensibly, certain highly profitable longer routes will be joined up—the London to Brighton, for example, in England.
claims.description: Motor roads will be joined into long-distance trunk routes, such as London to Brighton.

claims.quote: it is perhaps more probable they will be made of very good asphalt sloped to drain, and still more probable that they will be of some quite new substance altogether
claims.description: The motor roads will be paved with drained asphalt or some new material and used only by rubber-tired vehicles.

claims.quote: Their traffic in opposite directions will probably be strictly separated
claims.description: Motor roads will be divided highways with traffic in opposite directions kept apart.

claims.quote: where their ways branch the streams of traffic will not cross at a level but by bridges.
claims.description: Motor roads will use grade-separated junctions, with branching traffic crossing on bridges (interchanges).

claims.quote: once they exist it will be possible to experiment with vehicles of a size and power quite beyond the dimensions prescribed by our ordinary roads
claims.description: Wide motor roads will allow much larger and more powerful vehicles than ordinary roads permit.

claims.quote: it may be that some at least of the railway companies will hasten to replace their flanged rolling stock by carriages with rubber tyres, remove their rails, broaden their cuttings and embankments, raise their bridges, and take to the new ways of traffic.
claims.description: Some railway companies may tear up their rails and convert their lines into roads for rubber-tired vehicles.

claims.quote: woo the passenger back with carriages beautifully hung and sumptuously furnished, and all the convenience and luxury of a club.
claims.description: Railways may compete by widening gauges and offering smooth, club-like luxury carriages.

claims.quote: It is difficult to imagine, for example, how any sort of road-car organization could beat the railways at the business of distributing coal and timber and similar goods
claims.description: Road haulage will not beat railways at carrying bulk goods such as coal and timber.

claims.quote: Almost all will probably be still in existence and in divers ways busy, spite of the swarming new highways I have ventured to foreshadow, a hundred years from now.
claims.description: Railways will be modified and specialized rather than replaced, and most lines will still operate in a century.

claims.quote: And step by step with these developments will come a very considerable acceleration of the ferry traffic of the narrow seas through such improvements as the introduction of turbine engines.
claims.description: Turbine engines will make ferries across narrow seas much faster.

claims.quote: I hope at a later stage to give some reasons for anticipating that the centripetal pressure of the congested towns of our epoch may ultimately be very greatly relieved
claims.description: Crowded cities will eventually spread outward, relieving central congestion.

claims.quote: These things may be the first beginning of a process of restriction that may go far.
claims.description: City traffic will be increasingly regulated, with types of vehicle banned from streets at certain hours.

claims.quote: There is, however, one conceivable means of transit that is not simply frequent but continuous, that may be joined or left at any point without a stoppage, that could be adapted to many existing streets at the level or quite easily sunken in tunnels, or elevated above the street level
claims.description: Moving platforms of stepped speeds, reaching about 28 miles an hour, will run continuously through city tunnels or on elevated lines, with seats and bookstalls.
